Definition: from κεντέω (to prick); a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse):--prick, sting.
BiblicalUsage: Kentron means a sting, a prick, a goad: Acts 26:14 has the Lord saying to Saul, it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks: 1 Corinthians 15:55 cries, O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? 1 Corinthians 15:56 says the sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law. Revelation 9:10 says the locusts had stings in their tails, and their power was to hurt men five months.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sting is sin, and the goad is God: Saul kicked against the pricks until the Lord stopped him, and death's sting is pulled out at the resurrection. I hold that the victory song is already written, and the grave has no answer to it.
